newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Renault must follow EC rules on closure.
newsitem.headline: Renault must follow EC rules on closure.

text.p: The European Commission said on Friday that French car company Renault SA was obliged to go through "the correct procedure" in closing its Belgian plant, but it was up to individuals, trade unions or a member state to press the issue.

Barbara Nolan, spokeswoman for social affairs commissioner Padraig Flynn told Reuters that two European directives were in force to ensure the proper procedure was followed in the event of a multinational closing.
"One of these deals with collective redundancies and the other is part of the European works council directive," she said.
She said it was down to workers, trade unions or the Belgian state to take action if they believed Renault was closing the Vilvoorde plant without due consultation.
The decision by Renault to shut the plant caused a storm of protest from Belgium and unions on Friday but it cheered the stock market.

Investors welcomed news of what they saw as Renault getting to grips with its relatively high cost structure and boosted the shares more than 10 percent. That came on top of a five percent gain made on Thursday when the closure was announced.

But Belgian officials and newspaper were shocked at the death sentence for the plant. Car workers at Vilvoorde near Brussels, the home town of Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene, blocked the factory and prevented finished cars from leaving.
Nolan said if Renault had not followed procedures -- and the Commission was not passing judgement -- it was not the Commission's responsibility.
"On social affairs we deal with member states, not companies," she said.
